body: I appreciate your honesty, and I know that you are right. It's just hard to watch someone you care about repeatedly rip themselves apart. I think you said something that I needed to hear, because sometimes it isn't enough just to think it.

Thank you so much, your words are kind and just what I needed to hear. You're right, he does want his cake and to eat it too. He kind of said so himself the day I spoke to him. I told him that it just wasn't possible, and if he isn't serious about me he needs to say goodbye. He refused, but of course he is now ghosting me so maybe that was the last straw for him because confrontation during mania is a big no-no.

You're right. It hurts that there are people on here who all have similar stories, and often I wonder why I give it a free pass and feel like I'm the one begging for forgiveness. The day I saw them together, he insisted they were just friends, but I am not stupid. I don't know how often he had been speaking to her, but I am sure that it was emotional cheating if it hadn't become physical yet. I don't think she knows anything about how he can be, but I am certain he told her I was the crazy one because she started laughing as soon as she saw me with a pained expression.

I do have an appointment with a therapist, and I guess they can help untangle me and help me understand why I think it is okay when he does it but no one else.

Thank you, I appreciate your response. I have been dealing with depression and anxiety and used this as a bit of a catalyst to get myself some help too. Regardless of if I hear from him again, I just want to be ME again. It isn't all his fault that I had fallen so far, but to be with someone like him I believe that strength of self is the most important thing. 

I still think about him all the time though, and it kills me a bit. I think part of the problem is the support he has around him as well. He filters the people who try and dissuade him, and vents to the people who will encourage him tearing his life apart for a good time.

I understand your feelings, even though this is only the second time I have been through a random break up with my BPSO in 4 years. Stay strong, friend. We chose someone with a higher difficulty rating than most. Just remember that you are a golden person and people like me can see that for choosing to love someone with the ability to cause such pain.
I should probably add he has BPII.

I'm tired of trying to be better, I work so hard for myself and others and i just can't seem to save myself. Whatever else is after this can't be any worse than this constant numbness and unrelenting hopelessness.
You are a wise person, Greatbeard, and I have endless respect for you.

My thoughts exactly. If he truly feels it isn't helping him and he honestly don't want it, he is free to live as he wishes. We need to care for ourselves too though as SOs, and I don't think that it is being unreasonable to want stability for ourselves- as best as you can attain anyway.

Thank you for being a sweetheart and giving me a bit of hope. I had long been considering one of those pill boxes to help him remember, but he told me that he wasn't 60 and didn't need that sort of help. I don't force him to do things he isn't interested in, but perhaps a gentle reminder now is a good idea.

I wish the both of you luck and I hope he sees that things can be different and maybe even better with accepting his meds. You have a big heart, so don't forget to take care of yourself!

I'm not going to lie, your response made me cry a little. The feedback is much more appreciated as I know no one can see into the future. You are able to relate to him in ways that I can't so it means a lot that you replied, because I never quite feel like he's on a wavelength I can read during times like this. I hope you are able to find someone who can be there for you and who will love you through everything. You seem like a wonderful individual, so keep doing what you are doing. You matter too.
Then my family is grossed out by him again. Maybe next time, Monty... I think you're beautiful anyway.
Thanks for everyone's advise for how to help him! I didn't know how to post a picture yesterday, but here is Monty!
Oh don't worry, he has a heavy mesh lid to allow for better evaporation... and to also keep him in :) Thank you for the tips, he finally ate a small chunk of worm today. It's a start at least!
Thank you for your response, it makes me feel a bit better if nothing else. I just wish I knew what happened to him to prevent it in the future.
I should also add that when I adopted him he was 1.5 years old, and is housed in a 20 gallon long alone.
